lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The roles are not in reverse-chronological order; Harbor Payments should appear before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: Recruiters often scan dates before reading bullets.

items.says: The transition between diesel mechanics, operations, and product management is not obvious.
items.because: The roles may otherwise appear disconnected, especially for product applications.

items.says: Several bullets wrap awkwardly and are harder to scan.
items.because: The breaks make them look longer.

items.says: Verify that the URL is an actual professional profile rather than a placeholder.
items.because: The profile should reflect the product, operations, and analytics experience emphasized here.

items.says: Consider adding a current location or relocation indicator.
items.because: The education, work, and project locations vary.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA graduation date is accurate and the degree is completed or expected.
items.because: The current job begins immediately after the listed graduation date.

items.says: Add a relevant concentration, distinction, or coursework if applicable.
items.because: It could make the education more relevant to target roles.

items.says: Make the product or analytics connection more apparent in the MBA positioning.
items.because: The work history spans logistics, mechanical work, and product.

items.says: Clarify whether under five days per job was an average, target, or consistently achieved result.
items.because: The wording could make the result sound universal.

items.says: Add the business consequence of reduced dry-dock time if available.
items.because: Vessel availability, avoided delays, or operating capacity would show its impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the 14 vessels were your direct responsibility.
items.because: They could instead represent the entire company fleet.

items.says: The bullet shows responsibility but not impact.
items.because: Logging records alone is less persuasive than an inspection or maintenance outcome.

items.says: Add the scale of the hydraulic maintenance work.
items.because: The number of systems, service volume, or inspection frequency would establish scope.

items.says: Explain what the service records enabled.
items.because: Successful inspections, compliance, faster audits, or improved tracking would show their value.

items.says: “Owned” is vague, and the meeting is described rather than an outcome.
items.because: The bullet does not say what changed because of the scorecards.

items.says: Clarify how many carriers, managers, or routes the scorecards covered.
items.because: The scope of the responsibility is unclear.

items.says: If there was no measurable outcome, emphasize the decisions the scorecards supported.
items.because: Decision-making responsibility is stronger than the existence of a meeting.

items.says: Add the time period for the 30% reduction in pick errors.
items.because: The timing of the result is unclear.

items.says: Include the baseline or approximate pick volume if available.
items.because: It would make the scale of the reduction clear.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction was sustained and applied equally at both sites.
items.because: The current result does not establish either point.

items.says: Define S&OP on first use for generalist recruiters.
items.because: They may not know the acronym.

items.says: Define the forecast-error metric and verify that both figures use the same calculation.
items.because: The meaning and comparability of 18% and 11% are unclear.

items.says: Consider whether “12 consecutive quarters” is needed alongside “quarterly.”
items.because: The phrasing is somewhat repetitive unless the duration establishes ownership and continuity.

items.says: The bullet packs rollout, procedures, training, and negotiation into too many clauses.
items.because: That makes it difficult to scan and obscures the most relevant contribution.

items.says: Add rollout adoption, timing, route efficiency, service levels, or cost impact if available.
items.because: Those details would better establish the implementation’s result.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 annual driver hours were calculated and whether they were estimated or measured.
items.because: The basis of the savings figure is unclear.

items.says: Clarify which initiatives produced the driver-hour savings.
items.because: The current wording leaves attribution among the tool, procedures, and vendor negotiation unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether both the 9-day and 4-day figures are medians and how the control and pilot were measured.
items.because: The comparison needs a clear measurement basis.

items.says: Report effects on completion, verification failures, support contacts, or activation if available.
items.because: Time to first payment is the only outcome shown.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team’s if the redesign was collaborative.
items.because: Individual ownership is unclear.

items.says: Give the test duration and statistical reliability if available.
items.because: The scope and strength of the conversion result need clarification.

items.says: Clarify whether the 40,000 sessions were balanced across variants.
items.because: Total sessions alone do not establish that.

items.says: Define what “all merchants” means relative to the pilot.
items.because: It could mean a platform-wide launch or a defined segment.

items.says: Differentiate this checkout-test bullet from the later one.
items.because: Both report the same test result.

items.says: Add the decision or outcome produced by the RICE prioritization.
items.because: The bullet currently ends at the method.

items.says: Explain why support tickets closed was used to score Reach.
items.because: That is not the conventional interpretation in every RICE model.

items.says: Consider whether this work warrants a full bullet if it led to no shipped decision or measurable result.
items.because: More consequential work may deserve the space.

items.says: Define RICE on first use if readers may not know it.
items.because: It is an uncommon acronym for some audiences.

items.says: The bullet is overloaded with research, analysis, modeling, and roadmap work.
items.because: Readers may struggle to identify the main contribution.

items.says: Add the result of the roadmap decision.
items.because: The selected feature, expected impact, or approval would show that the priority mattered.

items.says: Clarify what “loss by segment” measures.
items.because: It could mean chargeback loss, operational cost, or another financial measure.

items.says: Session-level randomization does not by itself support the claimed effect on individual merchants’ customers.
items.because: The immediate measured outcome is session-level conversion, not necessarily a customer-level causal effect.

items.says: Add statistical significance, confidence intervals, or test duration if available.
items.because: Those details would strengthen the measurement account.

items.says: Remove or differentiate this bullet from the earlier checkout-test bullet.
items.because: The earlier bullet already reports the result, making this one repetitive.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned the recommendation, analysis, rollout plan, or presentation.
items.because: Your individual role is unclear.

items.says: Add the eventual scope or result of the funded regional rollout if available.
items.because: Approval alone does not show the later outcome.

items.says: Clarify your role relative to the student venture team.
items.because: It is unclear which parts of discovery, development, launch, partnerships, or operations you led.

items.says: Tie “in its first year” to a clear launch period.
items.because: The time frame is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain how the 9-tonne figure was measured and what it represents.
items.because: Collected, redistributed, and estimated diverted food are different measures.

items.says: Define what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: They could be users reached, registered users, or the target population.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The stated growth percentage is mathematically incorrect.

items.says: Clarify the period over which weekly active users increased.
items.because: The timing of the growth is unclear.

items.says: Clarify how the interviews informed the reminders without implying they alone caused the increase.
items.because: The causal wording is slightly ambiguous.

items.says: Add retention or repeat-use data if available.
items.because: Weekly active users can rise temporarily after a feature launch.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 26.7%.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and whether the fill-rate improvement was sustained.
items.because: The bullet establishes neither.

items.says: Explain how the volunteer shift system affected operations.
items.because: Its effect on capacity, staffing reliability, or demand matching is unclear.

items.says: Add the major assumptions or basis of the savings model.
items.because: The $2.4M estimate could otherwise seem inflated.

items.says: Clarify your individual role in the model, process analysis, or client recommendation.
items.because: Your contribution to the team effort is unclear.

items.says: Keep pilot funding distinct from realized savings.
items.because: Funding approval does not mean the estimated savings occurred.

items.says: Replace the passive wording with a clearer account of your role.
items.because: The bullet does not clearly show what you did.

items.says: Add the operational outcome of shortening the intake form.
items.because: Completion time, errors, throughput, or patient experience would show impact.

items.says: Quantify staff adoption or implementation if possible.
items.because: “Adopted by front-desk staff” does not establish its extent.

items.says: Give this bullet a distinct outcome if it overlaps the other practicum process-improvement bullets.
items.because: The scheduling and intake themes may feel duplicative.

items.says: Differentiate this pilot approval from the first practicum bullet or remove the weaker mention.
items.because: Both bullets say the client approved or funded a pilot.

items.says: Specify audience size or decision authority if it adds meaningful context.
items.because: It could clarify the significance of the presentation.

items.says: Add results from the 90-day pilot if available.
items.because: Results would be more valuable than approval alone.

items.says: Order the product skills for the roles being targeted.
items.because: Product management, experimentation, discovery, and requirements work should be easy to find.

items.says: Consider adding prioritization or stakeholder management if space allows.
items.because: The experience section can support those skills.

items.says: The tool list is underdeveloped; specify meaningful proficiency or use.
items.because: The list gives little detail about Excel, Jira, or Amplitude.

items.says: Add other relevant tools only if you have used them and can discuss the work.
items.because: The list may omit useful analytics, survey, or prototyping tools.

items.says: Connect listed tools to experience or projects where possible.
items.because: Tools that appear nowhere in those bullets need to be genuinely relevant to the target role.
